clue.text: In conversation, nag perhaps is grating

indicators.note: conversation is speech, so the word is to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: a nag is an old horse; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: Someone's nagging in conversation is wearing on the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' reads as a verb for pestering, but it is the noun for a worn-out horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, rasping voice is described as hoarse, a harsh sound like grating metal.

clue.text: Drink offering cold comfort?

blocks.note: surface reading: a beverage that offers little consolation, as in the phrase cold comfort
setter's reading: comfort for someone suffering from a cold, from a warming drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold comfort' is an idiom for poor consolation; read literally it is relief for a head cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot toddy is whisky with hot water, honey and lemon, a traditional home remedy taken for a chill.

clue.text: One wearing green with silver trim, going well together

indicators.note: something worn is put on around you, so the numeral sits inside the colour
a trim is an edging, so the metal borders the rest on both sides

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in green with silver edging is getting on nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside GREEN, and the silver symbol is split round the outside as a border.
explanation.definitionFit: Things in accord are harmonious and compatible, so they suit one another and are in agreement.

clue.text: Thin, asinine grin displayed in Hollywood musical

indicators.note: displayed in suggests the letters are laid out in a new arrangement on show

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A star flashes a vacant, silly smile throughout a Hollywood musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Singin' in the Rain is the 1952 MGM film starring Gene Kelly, famous for its song-and-dance numbers.

clue.text: Soldier getting into old woman's starter of entrails, wanting seconds and offal dishes

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece sits within another
a starter comes at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: a hag is an ugly old woman; the possessive supplies the S
GI is an American private soldier
the first letter of entrails
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A soldier raids a crone's kitchen while she prepares an offal starter, wanting second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier sits inside the old woman's to form the Scottish dish, which is sheep's offal cooked in a stomach; 'seconds' is the abbreviation, not more food.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is the traditional Scottish pudding of minced sheep's heart, liver and lungs, so several of them are plural offal-based meals.

clue.text: Primarily: 'Agreed! Manifestly! Endorsed! Naturally!'

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of the four exclamations

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic supporter fires off a string of emphatic yeses.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string of exclamations is both the source of the letters and the definition, a chorus of assent.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the end of a prayer to mean so be it, and casually as an expression of hearty assent.

clue.text: We don't weigh thin comic for Hollywood drama

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the letters are made to play about in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Slim actors insist they are too light for a comic role in a Hollywood film.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone with the Wind is the 1939 epic film of the American Civil War starring Vivien Leigh and Clark Gable.

clue.text: He painted horses, mostly fat, on a ship

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: stubby means short and thick, then shortened by its last letter
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An artist's horse paintings are mostly of plump animals aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was the eighteenth-century English artist celebrated above all for his portraits of racehorses.

clue.text: Some caused a terrifying calm

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: sits across caused, a and terrifying

explanation.surface: A frightening event ended up producing a strange stillness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate as an adjective means composed and unhurried, quietly serene in manner.

clue.text: Stir an army, to some extent, somewhere in Albania

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so the answer is a part of the words that precede it

blocks.note: sits across stir, an and army

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser stirs up troops somewhere in the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania, so it is one place within that country.

clue.text: Spooner's fervent penguin perhaps gets soy paste

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

blocks.note: fervent means eager or keen
a penguin is one kind of bird
swap the opening sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic penguin is rewarded with a dollop of soy paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd is another name for tofu, a soft paste-like block pressed from soya milk.

clue.text: Before start of Epsom, support horse that's old (13-19 years)

definitions.note: the bracket narrows 'old' to an age range

indicators.note: before means the earlier pieces come ahead of the letter that follows
a start is the beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a nag is an old horse
the first letter of Epsom

explanation.surface: At Epsom racecourse, a punter backs an ageing horse before the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is an English racecourse home of the Derby, which makes horse and support look like racing talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage describes the stage of life from thirteen to nineteen, the years whose numbers end in -teen.

clue.text: 'A fancy ship'? That's a joke

blocks.note: a means one
a liner is a grand passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a luxurious ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short quip delivered in a single sentence, a kind of brief jest.

clue.text: Lousy fool about to show respect? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary means the other way round, so the respectful word is turned backwards
about means around, so the fool wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: tit is a British slang word for a fool
to bow is to show respect by bending

explanation.surface: A rotten idiot is on the verge of showing deference, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal, and 'On the contrary' flips the respectful word before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is American slang for cheap or worthless, from a quarter dollar, so it means shoddy.

clue.text: Expected to be amazed when taking in little island

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the first piece encloses the second

blocks.note: awed means filled with wonder
an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A visitor is predicted to be astonished on reaching a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: AIT, a small river island as on the Thames, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awaited is anticipated or looked forward to, so it was foreseen as coming.

clue.text: You're telling me to wink and nod manically before Congress

indicators.note: doing something manically means wildly and chaotically, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
it is a coy slang word for sex, and congress can mean sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: A conspirator is told to wink and nod frantically ahead of a vote in Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the American legislature, but here it is the old word for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms of emphatic agreement, said when someone states something the speaker already knows only too well.

clue.text: Poultry served in beer for hoodlum

indicators.note: something served in a drink is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
a capon is a castrated cockerel raised for the table

explanation.surface: A gangster's dinner is chicken cooked in beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era, a famous gang boss.

clue.text: Reminders of monsieur being passionate, stone me!

indicators.note: being passionate means getting worked up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur
taken as written

explanation.surface: An excitable Frenchman exclaims at his souvenirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Mementos are keepsakes or souvenirs kept to recall a person or event.

clue.text: I'll eat gelato endlessly, voraciously (it's Italian fare)

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter of the last word is dropped
eating voraciously means wolfing things down chaotically, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the words as written, with the last letter of gelato removed

explanation.surface: A greedy diner promises to gobble up the ice cream at an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing O of gelato goes before the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagliatelle is a ribbon-shaped pasta from northern Italy, a classic dish of that country's cooking.

clue.text: Isn't honest with banks

blocks.note: first meaning: deceives someone by pretending
second meaning: steep cliffs or riverbanks

explanation.surface: Someone deceives the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluff is to feign confidence to mislead, while bluffs as a noun are steep headlands or banks.

clue.text: Said 'Full!' having swallowed a bit of tomato

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other
a bit of means a small part, here the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: sated means filled to satisfaction
the first letter of tomato

explanation.surface: A diner declares they are stuffed after just a morsel of tomato.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated is the past tense of state, to declare or express in words.

clue.text: Mostly regressive rule suppressing the theologian

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
regressive means going backwards, so the word reads from right to left
suppressing means holding down or keeping in, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: the word without its final letter, then turned round
taken as written

explanation.surface: A repressive regime silences a religious scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther was the German monk and scholar of divinity whose writings launched the Protestant Reformation.

clue.text: Injured veteran English respect

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A wounded old soldier earns the honour of the English.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to regard with deep reverence and esteem, a stronger form of honouring someone.

clue.text: Goes with 'Look up!'

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
to look is to see

explanation.surface: Someone sets off while being told to raise their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' means leaves, but it is the informal sense of passing water; a wee is British slang for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: Wees, as a verb, is informal British slang for urinates, and to go is a euphemism for that.

clue.text: A German refused caffeinated concoction: 'This is not skinny'

indicators.note: something refused is turned away, so those letters are taken out
a concoction is a mixture, so the remaining letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: ein is German for a
taken as written

explanation.surface: A German customer turns down a caffeinated drink, objecting that it is not a skinny one.
explanation.walkthrough: EIN comes out of caffeinated, leaving CAFFATED to scramble. 'Skinny' is coffee-shop talk for skimmed milk, but here it means thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a plump, round face cannot be called thin, so the whole sentence works as a definition.

clue.text: Eat too much, and sulk about hollow icing

indicators.note: about means around, so the sulking word wraps round the other piece
something hollow has had its middle removed, so only the outside letters stay

blocks.note: to pout is to sulk with pushed-out lips
the first and last letters of icing

explanation.surface: A greedy child stuffs themself and sulks over a cake with too little icing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is an informal idiom for gorging on food greedily, like a hog at a trough.

clue.text: Seek damages about Scandinavians becoming members of African Union

indicators.note: about means around, so the legal action wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: to sue is to seek damages in court
Danes are Scandinavian people from Denmark

explanation.surface: Nordic people take legal action over their membership of an African body.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan belongs to the African Union, so its citizens are people of a country within that continental body.

clue.text: Slider prepared for lazy folk

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A playground slide is made ready for the idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlers are people who avoid work and laze about, so they are indolent people.
